body_md: `Vec<T>` is a growable array on the heap. `vec![1,2]` macro or `Vec::new()` plus `push`. Index with `[0]`, iterate with `for x in &v`. Length via `len()`.
hook: Arrays are fixed — this list grows forever without realloc pain.

quiz.explain: Vec grows on heap; arrays have fixed length.

takeaway: Use Vec for growable same-type lists.
trap: Indexing past len panics; use get(i) for safe Option access.

body_md: Iterate without moving: `for x in &v` borrows, `v.iter()` same. Use `iter_mut()` to modify in place. Consuming `for x in v` moves the Vec.
hook: This for loop eats your Vec — unless you add one character.

quiz.explain: &v borrows so Vec stays usable after loop.
quiz.q: How do you loop without consuming Vec?

takeaway: Iterate by reference to keep ownership.
trap: Using v after `for x in v` errors; it was moved.

body_md: `String` is owned, growable UTF-8. `&str` is a borrowed view. Build with `String::from`, `to_string`, or `format!`. Never index Strings — use slices or chars.
hook: String vs &str confuses everyone — the difference is ownership.

quiz.explain: String owns heap text; &str borrows a view.
quiz.q: What is the String vs &str split?

takeaway: Own with String, borrow views with &str.
trap: Indexing String like s[0] fails; UTF-8 needs chars or slices.

body_md: Concatenate with `push` (char), `push_str` (&str), or `+` (consumes left). `format!` builds without taking ownership. `+` moves left operand — often surprising.
hook: a + b destroys a — string addition has a hidden move.

quiz.explain: + takes self by value, moving left String.
quiz.q: What does `a + b` do to String a?

takeaway: Prefer format! to avoid surprise moves.
trap: Reusing a after a + b gives moved-value error.

body_md: `HashMap<K,V>` stores key→value with `insert` and `get` (returns Option). `entry().or_insert()` handles upserts. Needs `use std::collections::HashMap;`.
hook: Counting words? This map method does it in one line.

quiz.explain: entry API inserts default only if key missing.
quiz.q: How do you increment-or-init a counter?

takeaway: Use entry API for get-or-create patterns.
trap: get returns Option; unwrapping missing key panics.
output:
{"a": 1, "b": 2}
// order varies run to run (HashMap has no stable order)

body_md: `?` propagates errors: on Err it returns early, on Ok it unwraps. Function must return Result. Add context with `map_err`. Keeps error paths one character long.
hook: Replace 10 lines of match with a single question mark.

quiz.explain: ? unwraps Ok or returns Err early.

trap: ? needs Result return type; mismatched error types need From.
output:
double("21") == Ok(42)
double("x") == Err(ParseIntError { kind: InvalidDigit })

body_md: `panic!` is for bugs that should crash (out-of-bounds, invariant broken). `Result` is for recoverable failures (file missing). Libraries return Result; never panic on user input.
hook: panic vs Result: pick wrong and your library gets 1-star reviews.

quiz.explain: panic crashes; Result lets caller recover.
quiz.q: When do you use panic vs Result?

takeaway: Panic for bugs; Result for expected failures.
trap: Unwrapping user input panics in prod; propagate Result instead.

body_md: Split code with `mod foo;` loading `foo.rs` or `foo/mod.rs`. Control visibility with `pub`. Import with `use crate::foo::bar;`. Encapsulation defaults to private.
hook: Everything private by default — unlocking it takes one keyword.

quiz.explain: Items are private unless marked pub.

takeaway: Modules default private; expose with pub.
trap: Forgetting pub on fn gives `private module` import error.
output:
hi
// two-file crate (main.rs + util.rs); needs `cargo run`, not single-file rustc

body_md: Mark fns with `#[test]`, assert with `assert_eq!`. Run `cargo test`. Unit tests live in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` beside code; integration tests in `tests/`.
hook: Tests live next to your code — no separate framework needed.

quiz.explain: cargo test builds and runs #[test] fns.

takeaway: Write #[test] fns and run cargo test.
trap: Forgetting assert_eq arg order; actual vs expected confusion in output.
output:
running 1 test
test it_adds ... ok
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed

body_md: `cargo fmt` formats code canonically. `cargo clippy` lints 600+ pitfalls like needless clones. Run both in CI. Fix warnings before review — they catch real bugs.
code:
$ cargo fmt --check
$ cargo clippy -- -D warnings
# fix: cargo fix --allow-dirty
hook: Two commands make your code look senior instantly.

quiz.explain: fmt formats, clippy lints for idioms and bugs.
quiz.q: What do fmt and clippy do?

takeaway: fmt for style, clippy for correctness lints.
trap: Ignoring clippy pedantic clones; they hide perf issues.
output: # fmt --check passes silently when clean; clippy -D warnings denies all lints

body_md: `Vec::get(i)` returns `Option<&T>` instead of panicking. `pop` removes last, `remove(i)` shifts. Pre-size with `Vec::with_capacity(n)` to avoid reallocs in hot loops.
hook: v[99] crashes — get(99) politely says None.

quiz.explain: get returns Option, avoiding panic on bad index.
quiz.q: Safe way to index a Vec?

takeaway: Prefer get over indexing for fallible access.
trap: remove(0) on large Vec is O(n); use VecDeque for queues.

body_md: Strings are UTF-8: `len()` counts **bytes**, `chars().count()` counts glyphs. Never slice blindly — use `chars()`, `lines()`, or `char_indices()` for safety.
hook: hello.len() is not 5 here — bytes vs characters strikes again.

quiz.explain: len is bytes; é takes 2 bytes in UTF-8.
quiz.q: What is len vs chars for "héllo"?

takeaway: len is bytes; chars counts Unicode scalars.
trap: Byte-slicing accented text panics; iterate chars instead.

body_md: `HashSet` tracks uniqueness; `BTreeMap` keeps keys sorted. `VecDeque` is a double-ended queue. Pick by access pattern: uniqueness, ordering, or push/pop ends.
hook: HashMap is not always the answer — two cousins beat it often.

quiz.explain: BTreeMap iterates keys in sorted order.

takeaway: Match collection to ordering and uniqueness needs.
trap: Iterating HashMap expecting order; order is randomized.
output: // compiles clean, no output — s holds {1}, b maps 2 -> "x"

body_md: `Result` combinators `map`, `and_then`, `map_err`, `unwrap_or` mirror Option's. Convert Option↔Result with `ok_or` and `ok`. No nesting needed for chained fallible calls.
hook: Turn an Option into a Result in one call — no match required.

quiz.explain: ok_or converts Option to Result with error value.
quiz.q: How do you convert Option to Result?

takeaway: Bridge Option and Result with ok_or and ok.
trap: Using unwrap during conversion reintroduces panics.

body_md: Custom errors: define enum with `thiserror::Error` derive, or `anyhow::Result` for apps. Implement `Display` via derive. Use `#[from]` for auto-conversion with `?`.
hook: Stop using String as your error type — do this instead.

quiz.explain: thiserror for libs (typed), anyhow for apps (flexible).
quiz.q: Best error strategy for libraries vs apps?

takeaway: Typed errors for libs, anyhow for application code.
trap: Box<dyn Error> everywhere erases matchable error kinds.
